{

  "body": "**【What Changed】**

Added "IK Eligible" flag support to line build sub-steps. When a garnish sub-step's component/customization option has the new "Machine Eligible" attribute set to Yes, an "IK Eligible" checkbox appears (default true). Added validation, change history tracking, and exposed the flag via recipe-service-v2 API to KDS.

Main changes:

1. Added `is_ik_eligible_selected` field to line build procedure step across domain model, internal-recipe-service interface, recipe-site interface, and recipe-service-v2 interface
1. Added `is_machine_eligible` field to `BOGetItemProcedureRelatedItemsResponse` for component/customization option mapping display
1. Added `IkEligibleMachineEligibleChecker` for save-time validation: sub-steps with IK Eligible=true must have linked component with Machine Eligible=Yes
1. Added "Machine Eligible" attribute init migration controller (`InitMachineEligibleAttributeController`)
1. Added IK Eligible to line build change history tracking

**【Affected Endpoints - recipe-service-v2 Interface】**

The `is_ik_eligible_selected` field was added to the procedure step view in the following response classes and their corresponding endpoints:

|Response Class|Endpoint|Method|
|---|---|---|
|`BulkGetItemStructureResponse`|`PUT /item/structure/bulk-get`|(Deprecated, WHISK)|
|`BulkGetItemLineBuildStructureResponseV2`|`PUT /v2/item/line-build/structure/bulk-get`|KCS|
|`BulkGetALLItemLineBuildBaseStructureResponse`|`PUT /item/all-line-build/base-structure/bulk-get`|KCS|
|`BulkGetItemLineBuildStructureResponse`|No direct REST endpoint (used internally by inventory consumable items view)|Internal|

**【Affected Functions】**

1. Line build create/edit page (garnish sub-step IK Eligible checkbox)
1. Line build save validation (Machine Eligible attribute check)
1. Line build change history
1. Line build JSON export/import
1. Recipe-service-v2 bulk-get endpoints (KDS consumption)
1. Machine Eligible attribute data migration (init controller)

**【Test Suggestions】**

1. Create line build: map a component item with Machine Eligible=Yes to a garnish sub-step, verify IK Eligible checkbox appears and defaults to true
1. Create line build: map a component item without Machine Eligible to a garnish sub-step, verify IK Eligible checkbox does NOT appear
1. Change mapping component: switch from Machine Eligible=Yes item to non-Machine-Eligible item, verify checkbox disappears and IK Eligible value is cleared
1. Save validation: set IK Eligible=true on a sub-step whose linked component lacks Machine Eligible=Yes, verify error message appears

"\*\*【What Changed】\*\*
Backend refactor that moves the IK Eligible flag (isIkEligibleSelected) from the sub-step (ProcedureStep) level to the step (Procedure) level on Item Line Build. Triggered when users save or validate a line build on a 41\* item edit page. Validation business rule is unchanged: a garnish step with IK Eligible = true requires at least one Machine Eligible component or customization option in any of its sub-steps; otherwise the save is blocked with the inline error "Missing attribute Machine Eligible."
Main changes:
1. Domain entity ItemLineBuild (live and snapshot) moves the field from Procedure.ProcedureStep to Procedure
1. All BO/AJAX/JSON request and response DTOs and their builders/mappers updated to read/write the field at the step level only (clean cutover, no dual-shape)
1. IkEligibleMachineEligibleChecker rewritten to iterate at Procedure level and check Machine Eligible across all child sub-steps (short-circuits on first failing step)
1. MongoDB migration script added on ItemVersionScript (MD-17820, autoBackup = true) — migrates item\*versions  item\*version\*variants only; item\*version\_snapshots is intentionally NOT migrated
1. Migration uses OR aggregation per procedure (TRUE wins, else FALSE if any FALSE present, else null) and handles both legacy line\*builds\*.procedures\* and current line\*builds\*\*.tasks\*\*.procedures\* shapes
\*\*Technical Details — Affected Code Sites\*\*
\*\*Domain entities:\*\* app.internalrecipe.item.linebuild.ItemLineBuild, app.internalrecipe.itemversionsnapshot.linebuild.ItemLineBuild
\*\*Validator:\*\* IkEligibleMachineEligibleChecker (iterates Procedure once; if procedure.activity == GARNISH AND isIkEligibleSelected == TRUE, requires any child sub-step to have Machine Eligible attribute)
\*\*BO DTOs (interface):\*\* BOReplaceItemLineBuildRequest, BOValidateLineBuildRequest, BOItemLineBuildHistoryRequest, BOGetItemLineBuildResponse, LineBuildCardView, BOItemLineBuildServiceBuilder
\*\*AJAX DTOs (recipe-site BFF):\*\* CreateItemLineBuildAJAXRequestV2, UpdateItemLineBuildAJAXRequestV2, ValidateItemLineBuildAJAXRequestV2, GetItemLineBuildAJAXResponseV2, ListItemLineBuildAJAXResponseV2, LineBuildCardAJAXView
\*\*Public bulk APIs (recipe-service-v2):\*\* BulkGetItemStructureResponse, BulkGetItemLineBuildStructureResponse(V2), BulkGetALLItemLineBuildBaseStructureResponse and their procedure builders
\*\*Adjacent flows:\*\* BOItemLineBuildErrorCheckServiceV2 (save/replace path), BOItemPackSizeReplaceBomValidateService (pack-size replace), Schedule40ModelReplaceUsageRequestBuilderPart2 (replace-usage), ItemRecipeLineBuildCopyHandler  ReplaceUsageRequestBuilder (copy/replace), BOGetChangeHistorySnapShotLineBuilderCardBuilder  ItemLineBuilderCardSnapShotBuilder (change history), Import/Export JSON V2 controllers
\*\*MongoDB migration:\*\* ItemVersionScript.migrateIkEligibleToStepLevel — runs on item\*versions and item\*version\_variants; per-document bulkWrite of set(step path)  unset(sub-step path); idempotent re-runs are no-ops; auto-backup enabled before mutation

30	**Main Scenario**
31	=================
32	
33	1. Clicking “Edit line build” link display edits line build page.
34	2. ‘Apply to restaurants’ dropdown for Non-customization Item: Add the Add ‘Apply to restaurants’ dropdown on this item’s Line Build.

38	3. When the “Multi versions vs options” or the “Is Multi-usage qty Item” toggle is on.
39	4. Click the ‘Create New line Build’ button and enter the “Editing line build information” page.
40	5. Add ‘Apply to restaurants’ dropdown list next to the ‘Apply to Option’ dropdown:
41	
42	   ![image-20250814-075856.png](../Attachments/4185031151/image-20250814-075856.png)
43	   1. Value: All, and each of the restaurant related to this Item;
44	   2. Once the 'All' is selected, other options should be grey out and unselect able.
45	   3. If the corresponding options updated, the drop-down list should also display all the latest options.
46	   4. Multiple choice. User can select one or multiple restaurants.
47	   5. Take the following as example, the possible cases are:
48	   6. Just Customizations:
49	   7. Line Build 1 (Option 1, Value A)
50	   8. Line Build 2 (Option 1, Value B )
51	   9. Just Restaurant ID
52	   10. Line Build 1 (Restaurant A)
53	   11. Line Build 2 (Restaurant B )
54	   12. Multiple Restaurant IDs
55	   13. Line Build 1 (Restaurant A, B, C)
56	   14. Line Build 2 (Restaurant D)
57	   15. Customizations & Restaurant
58	   16. Line Build 1 (Restaurant A, Option 1, Value A)
59	   17. Line Build 2 (Restaurant A, Option. 1, Value B)
60	   18. Line Build 3 (Restaurant B, Option 1, Value A)
61	   19. Line Build 4 (Restaurant B, Option 1, Value B)
62	   20. Line Build 5(Restaurant A, RestaurantB, Option1, ValueA)
63	   21. Line Build 6(RestaurantA, RestaurantB, Option1, ValueB)
64	6. Clicking save, we should do the following validation:
65	
66	   1. Once the “Apply to Option” is chosen, Option and option value is required. If user does not set, show error message:” Please set apply to option/option values”.
67	7. There must be a value in ’Apply to Option’. If user does not set, show error message:” Please set apply to Apply to Option values”.
68	8. For the common restaurants, we should use its default Line Build, which means the value of ‘Apply to Restaurants’ dropdown is ‘All’.
69	9. For the Exception Restaurants, user could create its Line Build by selecting the Restaurants Name in the ‘Apply to Restaurants’ dropdown.
70	10. We should check if the same Values on ‘Apply to Restaurants’& ‘Apply to Option’ and ‘Option Value’ already exists in the Item’s current Line Build version, if yes, user will get the tip: “This Line Build has already existed”, and let user choose to match the existing one. If no, the new Line Build could be generated.
71	11. For the new restaurants, the user must select a 'All' in the ‘Apply to restaurants’ dropdown when there isn’t a match version for new restaurants.
72	12. A recipe’s line build can have multiple steps. If the line build hasn’t been added, by default, show 3 empty steps.
73	13. Each step has these columns:
74	14. Order: an integer (1-99), user should be able to change the order by drag and drop.
75	15. Step: By default, it is the same as order. Should be an integer. Usually, if there are multiple steps mapping to the same option, the step should be the same.
76	16. Mapping option – option values: Setting mapping option – option value, means this step is only used/applicable if the customer order has selected this option value. If the customer does not select this order, it should not be shown on Chef App.
77	
78	    1. Mapping option lists all the options of this truck item. When no exact option is selected, “Option Value” list only has “Select an option value”. Once user selects an option, “Option value” should list all this options’ option values.
79	    2. Allow user to fuzzy search against customization option/item name in the dropdown list. Similar to 'Apply to restaurant' field.
80	
81	       1. Please add it for mapping option-option value, mapping option of task, apply to option/option value of line build as well.
82	    3. Remove the “Normal“  customization, today KDS will use the BOM Line Item instead
83	    4. Please note: after removed Normal option, the remove and extra can not be set in the step level, they only can be defined in sub step with mapped BOM item.
84	    5. Please note, “IsDefault Value“ will not be shown on the UI, but it will be sent to ChefApp.
85	    6. When send data to chef APP, for all ‘option – option value’s, we should also send Option type, IsDefault Value.
86	    7. If user select an option, but does not select an option value, when save, show error message: “Please select option value for step {step}”.
87	    8. Mapping option and option value should list as:
88	
89	|  |  |  |  |
90	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
91	| Option type | Option | Option value | IsDefault Value |
92	| Mandatory Choice | Option name | Option value name | Set it to “Y” if it is set as default |
93	| Optional Addition | Option name | Option value name | Set it to “Y” if it is set as default. |
94	| Dish Preference | Option name | Option value name | Set it to “Y” if it is set as default |
95	| On the side | Option name | 1. Option value name + “on the side” (option value ID = this option value’s ID) 2. Option value name + “NOT on the side” (option value ID = “-“ + on the side’s option value’s ID) | \*\* on the side = N  \*\* NOT on the side = Y |
96	
97	For example:

99	|  |  |  |
100	| --- | --- | --- |
101	| Option type | Option | Option value |
102	| Mandatory Choice | Burger Type | Plain  Whole wheat |
103	| Optional Addition | Spread | Butter  Honey |
104	| Dish Preference | Steak temperature | Raw  Middle  Well done |
105	| On the side | On the side | 1. Cheese on the side, option value ID = {OVID}, is default = N 2. Cheese NOT on the side, option value ID = -{OVID|, is default=Y |

107	17. Activity: Dropdown with the options listed below: Cook, Garnish, Complete, Vend.  Can’t be null. If null, error message: “Please select activity for step {order number list}”
108	18. Different Activities have different settings:
109	
110	    1. **Complete** - All recipes must have at least one completion step, there must only be one completion step
111	
112	       1. Mapping Option/Item
113	       2. Step Time must be greater than 0
114	       3. No: Cook Time & Resting Time Add a new parameter: Max Hold Time. Optional. Max Hold Time must be equal to greater than 0
115	       4. The appliance must be null
116	       5. Must have at-least one sub-step
117	       6. Must be the last step in the recipe
118	       7. Parking Spot: required, single select, possible option: Ambient, Warm. No default value. Placeholder: 'Make a selection…'
119	    2. **Cook:**
120	
121	       1. Must have an Appliance selected
122	       2. Step Time must be greater than Cook Time
123	       3. Cook Time must be greater than 0, no default value.
124	       4. Must have at least one sub-step
125	       5. max hold time: optional
126	       6. Appliance: Dropdown with the following options: C Vap, Clamshell Griddle, Fryer Basket, Hot Box, Microwave, Pitco, Pizza Conveyor Oven, Press, Rice Cooker, Steam Table, Toaster, Turbo Oven, Water Bath can be selected in Cook Activity. Sort the appliances by appliance name A~Z.
127	       7. If appliance= Steam Table,  C-VAP, show ‘Max Hold Time’: optional. Display it underneath ‘Cook Time’. It must be greater than 0, and it can be greater than 1 hour. User is able to set hours, minutes and seconds.
128	       8. Whatever the appliance is, show 'Max Hold Time' field, it is optional.
129	    3. **Garnish:**
130	
131	       1. Step Time must be greater than 0
132	       2. Cook Time & Resting Time must be equal to 0
133	       3. Must have at least one sub-step
134	    4. **Vend:**
135	
136	       1. Show the following fields: Order, Mapping Option, Option Value, Activity, Visual.
137	       2. Don’t show ‘cooking eligible’ checkbox in the sub step.
138	       3. 'Mapping Option/Item': required.
139	       4. Show 'Parking Spot' field for each sub step. If any sub-step with ‘Parking Spot'=null, show inline error message as the following screenshot.
140	19. Parameters
141	
142	    1. Step Time/Cook Time/Resting time: Two text 1) minutes 2) seconds: integer from 0 to 59. If it is required, should be greater than 0 second. For example, 1:00, 0:15 are both correct. If format is not correct, error message: “Step time/Cook Time/Resting time should be greater than 0 for step {order number list}.”
143	    2. Appliance: Dropdown with the following options: Turbo Oven, Water Bath, Hot Box. If activity is “Cook”, it is required. Error message:” Please select appliance for step {order number list}.”.
144	    3. ‘Water Bath’ is utilized during pre-service and then have items remain in the water bath to be hot held (rather than moving to hotbox). For example, the broth for chuko is re-thermalized in the water bath during Pre-Service.  Once the timer goes off, the COR leaves the item in the waterbath and then grabs it directly from the water bath when broth is part of an order.

Based on the ticket analysis, here is a comprehensive breakdown of how these five IK Eligible requirements evolve, with emphasis on what MD-18130 adds as new constraints:

---

## TIMELINE & PROGRESSION

**MD-17690** (Created 2026-04-08, Done 2026-04-21) — IK Support - IK Eligible Line Build
**MD-17820** (Created 2026-04-24, Done 2026-04-27) — Move IK Eligible flag from sub-step to step level
**MD-17947** (Created 2026-05-15, Done 2026-05-27) — Enable IK Eligible for Cook Steps
**MD-17982** (UI subtask of MD-17947) — tracking UI implementation
**MD-18130** (Created 2026-06-18, Done 2026-07-10) — NEW: Machine eligibility warning + step ordering constraint

---

## FOUNDATION (MD-17690)

**Title:** IK Support - IK Eligible Line Build

**Key Requirements:**
1. Add new "Machine Eligible" attribute (dropdown type, Master Data domain, sub-attribute)
2. Show "IK Eligible" checkbox on garnish steps when mapped component has Machine Eligible=yes (defaults to true, user can uncheck)
3. When customization option is mapped with sub-step of garnish activity, show checkbox if any mapping item has Machine Eligible=yes
4. Validation: If IK Eligible=true but linked component lacks Machine Eligible=yes, block save with inline error: "Missing attribute Machine Eligible"
5. When changing mapped component, show/hide checkbox and clear previous IK Eligible value accordingly
6. Track IK Eligible flag in line build change history
7. API: Return IK eligible value + item number/menu item usage to KDS in recipe-service-v2 endpoints

---

## STRUCTURAL REFACTOR (MD-17820)

**Title:** Move IK Eligible flag from sub-step level to step level

**What Changed:**
The `is_ik_eligible_selected` field moved from `ProcedureStep` (sub-step) level to `Procedure` (step) level. This was a clean data model restructuring, not a business logic change.

**Updated Requirements:**
- Show "IK Eligible" checkbox at garnish step level (no default value — user manually checks/unchecks)
- Hide checkbox when switching step activity to non-garnish, clear previous value
- Preserve existing validation: IK Eligible=true requires at least one Machine Eligible item/option in ANY child sub-step
- MongoDB migration applied to item_versions and item_version_variants; item_version_snapshots intentionally NOT migrated
- All BO/AJAX/JSON DTOs updated to read/write field at step level only (clean cutover, no dual-shape)
- Affected recipe-service-v2 endpoints: `PUT /item/structure/bulk-get`, `PUT /v2/item/line-build/structure/bulk-get`, `PUT /item/all-line-build/base-structure/bulk-get`

---

## ACTIVITY EXPANSION (MD-17947)

**Title:** Enable IK Eligible for Cook Steps

**What's New:**
Extended the IK Eligible checkbox from GARNISH-only steps to COOK steps as well.

**Key Requirement — Preserve Existing Configurations:**
"When a step is marked IK eligible, keep all existing activity step configurations. Like, cook steps: retain appliance, cooking time, and other cooking-specific fields. This ensures that if the item is NOT filled in the IK slot at the HDR, the CE can still cook it via a la minute instruction using the existing step configuration."

**Workflow Example (Steak):**
- If steak marked IK eligible on cook step with IK slot filled at HDR: steak is pre-cooked and filled into IK slot
- If IK slot NOT filled at HDR: CE cooks steak via existing a la minute instruction using cook step's appliance/cooking time
- No additional pre-cook steps auto-generated in line build (handled by SOP/offline training)

**Validation:**
- Validator activity guard changed from `activity != GARNISH` to `activity != GARNISH && activity != COOK`
- Existing machine-eligible check: step can be marked IK eligible only if at least one mapped item is Machine Eligible; otherwise save blocked

---

## NEW VALIDATIONS & CONSTRAINTS (MD-18130)

**Title:** IK Support - Component machine eligibility warning and IK step ordering constraint

**Rationale:**
Requested by Charlie Fox to reduce CE-team configuration errors. Only applies to WONDER_HDR restaurants and GARNISH/COOK steps with IK Eligible=true.

### Validation 1: Machine-Eligible Warning (WARNING level, NON-BLOCKING)

**When:** Saving a line build

**What to Check:**
For each step marked IK Eligible=true, verify that ALL mapped components/customization options have the Machine Eligible attribute.
- Component-mapped sub-steps: must have Machine Eligible attribute
- Option-mapped sub-steps: pass if at least one item under option is Machine Eligible
- Instruction-only sub-steps (no mapped component/option): ignored

**If Violation Found:**
Return a non-blocking warning (does not prevent save):
```
Are you sure?
Some components on IK Eligible steps are not Machine Eligible. Are you sure you want to save it?
Task ({task name}) - Step 1: {component item number} {component item name}; {option name1}; {option name2}.
Task ({task name}) - Step 2: {component item number} {component item name}; {option name1}; {option name2}.
[Action: Cancel, Save]
```

Also show persistent message in line build detail page bad-data section:
```
Title: Bad data exist in line build #1 task {task name}
Context:
1. Some components on IK Eligible steps are not Machine Eligible:
   Step 1: {component item number} {component item name}; {option name1}; {option name2}.
   Step 2: {component item number} {component item name}; {option name1}; {option name2}.
2. {other problem steps}
```

**Rationale for Warning (not Error):** Users can remove the Machine Eligible attribute from a component after the line build is saved, making an error unreliable. Warning is sufficient.

---

### Validation 2: IK Eligible Step Ordering Constraint (ERROR level, BLOCKING)

**Why This Matters:**
IK items must physically flow from machine to finishing station. IK super pods (machine) feed into hybrid pods (finishing station). All IK-eligible steps must be grouped at the start; any step needing finishing-station work must be non-IK-eligible (assigned to hybrid pod) and appear after all IK steps.

**When:** Saving a line build containing any IK Eligible=true step

**What to Check:**
For a task with IK-eligible steps:
1. All IK Eligible steps must appear FIRST in the task (before any non-IK steps)
2. All IK Eligible steps must be CONSECUTIVE (no non-IK steps between them)
3. Instruction-only steps (no mapped components/options) are disallowed before or between IK Eligible steps

**If Violation Found:**
Block save with error (hard constraint):
```
Unable to save line build: IK Eligible steps must come first and be consecutive, please move the below IK Eligible steps to the top of task(s).
• Task ({task name}) - Step 1, Step 4, Step 5
• Task ({task name}) - Step 1, Step 3
```

**Implementation Details:**
- Validate endpoint returns offending steps for UI display (non-blocking)
- BFF save flow (create/update) re-checks and throws ConflictException before persisting (hard error)
- COMPLETE steps are ignored by the ordering rule (can appear anywhere)
- Scope: WONDER_HDR restaurants only; GARNISH/COOK activities only

---

## SYNTHESIS: HOW MD-18130 BUILDS ON PRIOR WORK

**Layers of IK Eligible Implementation:**

1. **Layer 1 (MD-17690):** Basic IK Eligible checkbox on garnish steps, validation that at least one sub-step item is Machine Eligible (error-level enforcement)

2. **Layer 2 (MD-17820):** Moved checkbox from sub-step level to step level; refined data model; no business logic change

3. **Layer 3 (MD-17947):** Extended activity support from GARNISH-only to COOK steps; added requirement to preserve cook step configurations (appliance, cooking time) for a la minute fallback

4. **Layer 4 (MD-18130):** Added TWO NEW validations to reduce CE errors:
   - **Validation 1** strengthens the machine-eligible check: now requires ALL (not just one) mapped items to be Machine Eligible, surfaced as a warning message in save dialog and persisted bad-data area
   - **Validation 2** enforces step ordering: IK-eligible steps must come first and be consecutive within a task; steps cannot be interspersed with non-IK work; this is an ERROR-level constraint (blocks save)

**What MD-18130 Adds (NEW Requirements):**

1. A **WARNING-level validation** on save that does NOT block but alerts when mapped components lack Machine Eligible attribute; persists in UI bad-data section
2. An **ERROR-level validation** on save that enforces IK step ordering (first + consecutive); blocks save if violated
3. Both validations scoped to WONDER_HDR restaurants only (not all restaurants)
4. Machine-eligible warning explicitly handles option-mapped items (at least 1 Machine Eligible item under option suffices)
5. Clarifies that instruction-only steps are disallowed between/before IK steps (not just regular non-IK steps)

These validations reduce manual CE errors by catching configuration mistakes at save time, while warning-level approach allows users to override if they understand the risk (machine-eligible attributes can be changed post-save).

## Key Takeaways for Documentation Updates

1. **Progression:** The feature evolved from basic IK Eligible + Machine Eligible foundation (MD-17690) → data model refactor (MD-17820) → activity expansion (MD-17947) → now adding guardrails (MD-18130).

2. **MD-18130's New Impact:** Adds two validations:
   - **Machine-Eligible Warning** (non-blocking) — surfaced at save time, persistent in bad-data section
   - **IK Step Ordering Constraint** (blocking) — enforces physical pod workflow (super pod work first, then hybrid pod downstream)

3. **Scope:** Both new validations limited to WONDER_HDR restaurants only.

4. **8 Pages Modified:** 4 critical pages (IK Eligible definition, Machine Eligible definition, 2 new validation pages) + 4 important pages (flows, activity logic, data model, cook procedure).

5. **No new attributes or entities** — MD-18130 only adds validation rules on existing IK Eligible + Machine Eligible pair. The foundation was solid; MD-18130 hardens it against CE configuration errors.
